properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued July 28 at 4:14PM MDT until July 28 at 7:15PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
FFWPUB

The National Weather Service in Pueblo has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Middle and South Aspen Acres Burn Scar in...
East Central Custer County in southeastern Colorado...
West Central Pueblo County in southeastern Colorado...

* Until 715 PM MDT.

* At 414 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain over the Middle and South Aspen Acres Burn Scar. Up to
0.5 inches of rain have fallen on the western edge of the scar. The
expected rainfall rate is 1 to 1.5 inches in 1 hour. Additional
rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are possible in the warned area.
Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly. Excessive
rainfall over the burn scar will result in debris flow. The debris
flow can consist of rock, mud, vegetation and other loose
materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the Middle and South Aspen
Acres Burn Scar.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Middle and South Aspen Acres Burn Scar.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Rye, San Isabel, Beulah and Colorado City.

This includes the following high risk locations...
Beulah Water Intake.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued July 28 at 4:07PM MDT until July 28 at 6:30PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
At 407 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy
rain over the Northern Aspen Acres Burn Scar. Between 0.5 and 1.5
inches of rain have fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 1 to 2
inches in 1 hour. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to
begin shortly. Excessive rainfall over the burn scar will result in
debris flow moving through the North Creek, Red Creek, Peck Creek and
Rock Creek Drainages. The debris flow can consist of rock, mud,
vegetation and other loose materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the Northern Aspen Acres Burn
Scar.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Northern Aspen Acres Burn Scar.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of East Central Custer and West Central Pueblo
Counties.

This includes the following high risk locations...
Northcreek Road county line to Red Mountain Camp and Northcreek Road
from Red Mountain Camp to Beulah.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued July 28 at 12:13PM MDT until July 28 at 8:00PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding and debris flows caused by excessive
rainfall over the Gold Mountain Fire Burn Scar are possible.

* WHERE...Gold Mountain Fire Burn Scar in Ouray County Colorado,
including Dexter Creek and Cutler Creek, particularly along
highway 550, and Cow Creek.

* WHEN...Until 800 PM MDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Excessive rainfall is possible over the Gold Mountain
Burn Scar which could lead to flash flooding and/or debris flows,
particularly along highway 550 between Cutler Creek and Dexter
Creek. Cow creek may also be affected. The debris flow can consist
of rock, mud, vegetation and other loose materials.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1202 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Gold Mountain Burn Scar, including Cow Creek, and along
highway 550 between Cutler Creek and Dexter Creek.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
